sources.title: The ESSKA-AFAS international consensus statement on peroneal tendon pathologies.
sources.publicationStatus: Final journal publication; metadata firstPublicationDate 2018-05-16. Version/access details below.

access.details: Full publisher article and Europe PMC XML/reference trail inspected. Later correction body directly opened at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6829698/; corroborating author-institution record inspected. Institution PDF returned 403.

integrity.method: Publisher/PubMed records inspected during research; Europe PMC REST core metadata DOI:10.1007/s00167-018-4971-x rechecked during serialization, including publication type and comment/correction links. Not a registry-wide clearance.
integrity.result: Linked correction DOI 10.1007/s00167-018-5021-4 (PMID 29938307), https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6829698/, corrects two author names only; no clinical recommendation changes in this notice. Not an exhaustive integrity clearance.

sources.design: International multidisciplinary consensus based on scarce, heterogeneous evidence.
sources.population: Peroneal tendon pathologies; distinguish tendinopathy from tear, rupture and dislocation.
sources.coInterventions: Acute associated-injury management and symptom measures.
sources.outcomes: Consensus supports conservative care, painless weight bearing followed by ROM and tendon loading as appropriate. Dose is unvalidated. Conservative references include mixed-tendon PRP and luxation/subluxation reports, not an isolated-tendinopathy exercise RCT.
sources.uncertainty: Consensus rests on sparse evidence, including mixed-tendon and subluxation reports. It does not establish an isolated-tendinopathy exercise dose. Postoperative repair limits are a separate population.
sources.limitations: Consensus rests on sparse evidence, including mixed-tendon and subluxation reports. It does not establish an isolated-tendinopathy exercise dose. Postoperative repair limits are a separate population. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

protocol.execution: Weight bearing when painless, then ROM/tendon loading appropriate to diagnosis; no specific verified band exercise execution.
protocol.dose: not reported as validated specific exercise dose.
protocol.supervision: Clinically managed; no universal supervision schedule.
protocol.stoppingRules: Painless weight-bearing prerequisite in consensus rationale; no trial-based numeric exercise threshold.

sources.population: A 50-year-old woman with chronic lateral ankle symptoms consistent with peroneal tendinopathy.
sources.coInterventions: Orthotics, strengthening, manual therapy and home program; a lateral calcaneal glide was added.
sources.outcomes: Pain, function, heel raises and balance improved over eight visits; patient returned to work and recreational exercise.
sources.followUp: Eight visits; long-term durability not established in the abstract.
sources.uncertainty: Single case with multiple treatments and no comparator; exact home program and harms unavailable. Improvement cannot be attributed to strengthening alone.
sources.harms: not reported in the accessible abstract.
sources.limitations: Single case with multiple treatments and no comparator; exact home program and harms unavailable. Improvement cannot be attributed to strengthening alone. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

protocol.execution: reported in accessible text: Abstract describes peroneal strengthening, manual therapy and a structured home exercise program; lateral calcaneal glide was added. Exact strengthening technique, resistance and range are not described.
protocol.dose: reported in accessible text: Abstract observes improvement over eight visits. This is an observed visit count, not a reported weeks-long schedule, visits-per-week rate or per-exercise dose.
protocol.supervision: reported in accessible text: Abstract identifies a structured home exercise program alongside the treatment visits; the amount and arrangement of direct exercise supervision remain unreported.

sources.design: Retrospective service evaluation, n=27, principally a diagnostic/tenography study.
sources.population: Adults with mixed chronic peroneal disorders, including tendinosis and tears; median age 50.
sources.coInterventions: Boot/physiotherapy, selected band strengthening, tenography and escalated care.
sources.outcomes: Fifteen of 27 reported adequate pain relief after tenography. This is not an exercise efficacy estimate.
sources.uncertainty: Retrospective mixed-pathology series selected for diagnostic/interventional care. Band strengthening dose and isolated effect are unknown; tenography benefit is not exercise evidence.
sources.harms: Isolated exercise harms were not established.
sources.limitations: Retrospective mixed-pathology series selected for diagnostic/interventional care. Band strengthening dose and isolated effect are unknown; tenography benefit is not exercise evidence. Research candidate only; no clinical release.
